top.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
top.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. top.description: MUNCIE — Six times, Ball State 's offense had the ball inside Buffalo's 30-yard line. Six times, Ball State's offense came away with zero points. Ball State football was officially eliminated from bowl game contention with its seventh loss, falling 28-7 to Buffalo at home on Wednesday, Nov. 11 , in a rain-soaked midweek MACtion game. The Cardinals (3-7, 2-4 MAC) scored the first touchdown of the game after recovering a blocked punt in the end zone, then proceeded to score nothing else as the offense fell flat time and time again. More: Three takeaways from Ball State football's miserable loss to Buffalo Ball State head coach Mike Uremovich knew exactly where to place the blame for the offensive failures. "The loss falls on one person, and that's me," Uremovich said Wednesday. "I'm the offensive coordinator. I call the plays. We didn't score a touchdown, that's completely my fault. ... When you get down in the redzone and have to settle for field goals, I'm not calling the right plays, so if you're looking for somebody to blame for this game and the way it ended up at the end, you're looking at him." Despite taking the blame for Wednesday's loss, Uremovich will continue to serve as the offensive play caller. He told the media at Ball State's weekly pregame press conference on Friday, Nov. 13, that he had not considered making a change with play calling. "We're going to continue to do it exactly the way we've done it," Uremovich said. "I've got to do a better job in the red zone, and we have to execute better in the red zone. We moved the ball up and down the field, we spent a lot of time on their end of the field, a lot of time in the red zone and didn't get any points out of it." top.title: Giants’ Cam Skattebo calls out MetLife crowd after crushing loss
top.description: Giants running back Cam Skattebo had a rather eventful Thursday night. It ultimately ended in shocking disappointment, as the Giants blew a four-point lead in the final two minutes and lost 24-21 to the Commanders. This was a big-time missed opportunity for the Giants, who now don’t have the NFC East tiebreaker advantage over the Commanders. While the 5-3-1 Giants remain alone atop the division, they could have emerged from Thursday with a significant cushion as their schedule gets tougher. As for Skattebo, he wants to see — and hear — more from the crowd at MetLife Stadium, starting with next week’s home game against the imposing Jaguars. That nationally televised 4:25 p.m. game now looms large. There were some empty seats in the upper deck at MetLife on Thursday night. Skattebo noticed. “Everyone expected a thunderstorm and a dumping-rain game, so probably missing a couple people out there [because of that],” Skattebo said of the vibe. “But it turned out good, man. A lot of people on third down, making noise. I think this stadium could be a little bit louder when the defense is on the field at times in more critical moments. But at the end of the day, we’ve got to execute.” Yes, indeed. The Giants got the ball back with 2:15 left, up 21-17, on Washington’s 46 after an interception. This was the offense’s chance to seal the victory. “We wanted to end the game right there,” right guard Francis Mauigoa told NJ.com. But they went three plays and out, gaining just 5 yards in 29 seconds. A rare terrible punt from Jordan Stout (12 yards) gave the Commanders possession at their 29. They answered with the 71-yard, game-winning touchdown drive. “We had opportunities at the end of the game to close it out — and we didn’t,” Skattebo said. “We’ve just got to execute better.” Skattebo mostly played well after Giants coach John Harbaugh opted to not trade for Jonathan Taylor to replace him. top.title: Ravens update QB Lamar Jackson’s status after successful thumb surgery
top.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 01: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens takes the field for warmups prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens released a statement from head coach Jesse Minter on Friday morning that delivered the team’s first rough timeline on Lamar Jackson’s return from a thumb injury suffered 0n November 1. Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8. Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season. The statement is the most concrete update on Jackson’s status since he went down two weeks ago in Buffalo. However, it lacks the following information: Has Jackson undergone surgery on his thumb? If so, when? If not, when will he get surgery on his thumb? Is the given timeline based on when he suffered the injury, when the statement was released, or when he undergoes surgery? The first three questions were subsequently answered by ESPN’s Jamison Hensley and The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec, who both reported that Jackson has undergone surgery and is currently in the rehab process. It is somewhat baffling why the Ravens would not include that information in their statement. Presumably, the beat reporters who confirmed the surgery received their information from a team source. Why, then, couldn’t the team just say that Jackson had undergone successful surgery? Giving a precise date is not even necessary – the type of thing fans and media would love to know, but do not really need to. This story will be updated with more information.

top.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - APRIL 11: Forward Gavin Morrissey #7 of the Wisconsin Badgers shoots the puck during the NCAA Division I Men's Ice Hockey Championship game between Wisconsin Badgers and Denver Pioneers on April 11, 2026, at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. They sit atop the rankings for the second consecutive week while awaiting a visit from Ohio State this weekend. But before we get into Ohio State, let’s revisit last weekend’s trip to Minneapolis, shall we? No. 1 Wisconsin (7-0-1, 3-0-1 Big Ten) is cruising behind their two-headed monster in goal. Sophomores Alexis Cournoyer and Daniel Hauser are both benefiting from the timeshare in the crease, as the Badgers have posted three shutouts so far this season (four if you include the exhibition against Western Michigan). They’ve allowed just six goals since the start of the season. Cournoyer only conceded one goal against the Gophers, and it was in the waning seconds of a five-minute power play after Grady Deering was ejected for boarding in the first period. Hauser blanked Minnesota on Saturday night for his second shutout of the season, the first road shutout against Minnesota in 16 years. Through four starts, Hauser is now allowing just 0.50 goals per game, a steep decline from his counterpart, Cournoyer, who is allowing a whopping 0.98 goals per game in his four starts. top.title: Eagles down to 4 captains after starting the season with 7
top.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles started the 2026 NFL season having voted seven players as captains , and as we enter Week 10, the team’s bye, they are down to just four on the active roster. It’s remarkable how different this team looks halfway through the current campaign. Lane Johnson — Retired Jalen Hurts — Out indefinitely due to blood clots Jordan Davis — Traded to the Jaguars Three of the four remaining captains have had to show their leadership from the sidelines at many points this season, and been unable to contribute on the field. DeVonta Smith — Played in only 4 games, and hasn’t seen the field since Week 6. Saquon Barkley — Missed 2 games due to injury and returned in Week 7 on a pitch count. He suffered a new back injury early in his return, and has been on a closely monitored snap count in the weeks since. Zack Baun — Missed 1 game with a concussion. That leaves just Jordan Mailata as the only captain still on the Eagles active roster to have played in all nine of the team’s games ( and every single offensive snap! ) in 2026. The All-Pro left tackle’s voice and presence is more important than ever with the offensive line turning to younger, inexperienced players up front, and the group falling to one of the worst in the league. This season has been a huge disappointment, with the Eagles heading into their bye week riding a seven-game losing streak. Both sides of the ball have dealt with a long list of injuries, and there’s been little-to-no consistency on offense to allow for the new scheme to develop. The seven players voted as captains at the start of the season were picked by their teammates for a reason, and their leadership was expected to help shepherd a new system in Philly, but instead, the Eagles are down to just four captains and need new guys to step up.

top.title: Watch Dani Pedrosa’s Spiked MotoGP Bike Beat an F1 Car, a Rally Car, a Pro 4 Truck and a Snowmobile on a 107-Acre Frozen Lake
top.description: Dani Pedrosa won the first Red Bull Ultimate Winter Race on a MotoGP bike with custom spiked wheels, beating an F1 car, a rally car, a Pro 4 truck and a snowmobile on a course built across 107 acres of frozen lake in Eagle River, Wisconsin, according to a Red Bull release dated November 12. Red Bull Media House sent the release with a 16-minute YouTube video, embedded below,. Temperatures on the lake were -17 degrees Celsius. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HVScH48KGGA Video: Red Bull / YouTube The five entries Pedrosa rode a KTM RC16. Patrick Friesacher drove the F1 car, Scott Speed a Subaru WRX ARA 25, Andrew Carlson a Pro 4 truck and Gunnar Sterne a Ski-Doo 440 race sled, with Jeremiah Burton hosting. The release calls the F1 car “the Oracle Red Bull Racing car” and never gives a chassis. The video description names it as an RB7, the car Red Bull raced in 2011. Representative image: a 2011 Red Bull RB7. Photo: Calreyn88 / Wikimedia Commons (CC0) Speed is the lineup’s rally driver, in a sport where WRC has added Rally US to its 2027 calendar . Carlson’s truck is a V8 he puts at 950 horsepower in the video, and Red Bull has other off-road drivers on the payroll, such as Bryce Menzies, who we covered moving from Baja 1000 teammate to rival . How the course was set up The release says the track had shorter inside lines for the vehicles that don’t belong on ice and longer outside routes for the ones that do. Sterne, on the sled, ran the longest line. Carlson launched off a jump at the start. Every vehicle ran a calibration lap before the race. The video commentary says the five calibration laps landed within two seconds of each other, and that the rally car did its lap in 1:13. The sled carries about 400 studs and carbide skis; the commentators describe the MotoGP bike as having the largest spikes in the field and close to 300 horsepower. Friesacher says the F1 car got changes to tires and ride height for the cold, and that he would run longer spikes, like Pedrosa’s, next time. Representative image: a Pro 4 truck at Crandon, Wisconsin. Photo: Royalbroil / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0) The result Pedrosa credits the start. “My bike is one of the lightest vehicles, so I knew if I could gain a gap early, I could be more cautious through the turns,” he said in the release, adding that the tight turns made line choice the second key. The release says Friesacher finished “a close second” and gives no finishing order or times for anyone else. The video’s auto-generated captions are garbled at the finish and read as though the sled was second and the F1 car third, so we are only reporting what the release states. Margins are not given in either place, and the release’s line about where to watch the full race still has the word LINK in it. Representative image: Dani Pedrosa at the 2018 Thai Grand Prix, on a Honda. Photo: Box Repsol / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) The release does not say when the race was held. top.title: Concacaf Nations League USMNT vs. Haiti – first leg preview
top.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Round of 32 - United States v Bosnia and Herzegovina - San Francisco Bay Area Stadium, Santa Clara, California, U.S. - July 1, 2026 Weston McKennie of the U.S. celebrates after the match as United States qualify for the round of 16 stage of the World Cup IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/David Gonzales | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters The USMNT is set to take on Haiti in a match dripping with narrative. Mostly that’s around the departure of Mauricio Pochettino who has decided to take his talents to Manchester. This means the USMNT will be without their manager as of Tuesday immediately following the second match against Haiti in the Nations League. That Poch would leave while his project of “seeing the potential of our fans and all the people in this amazing country that is the USA, what they showed us during the World Cup. I think it’s an amazing opportunity to be bold, but to be part of creating, evolving and developing an amazing new…” BLAH, BLAH, BLAH, BLAH, BLAH. Behind those pretty words was the truth that Poch was a hired gun and found something he would rather do and get paid more for. That aside, there’s a soccer game being played in Miami which is standing in for Haiti’s home match in the two leg Concacaf Nations League schedule this international window. As far as what to expect, the USA under Poch is pretty well established. It will try to dictate the match by moving the ball quickly up field and try to breakdown Haiti’s likely low block. The core of the team is back for this window and getting a win in the first leg will be key for the Americans. Look for Chris Richards and whoever starts next to him to hold down the back line flanked by Antonee Robinson on the left and someone on the right playing behind Weston McKennie and Tyler Adams anchoring the midfield with maybe Malik Tillman, Jack McGlynn or Sebastian Berhalter joining. The attacking trio should see Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun make the XI with the third Musketeer possibly being Cavan Sullivan, Justin Ellis, or Julian Hall. Hopefully, whoever is between the sticks keeps it together for 90 minutes. Haiti is coming off of being bounced in the group stage of the World Cup but qualification for the first time in 50 years was a step forward for the program. They played catchup in most of their World Cup matches and struggled to balance holding a defensive shape and creating scoring chances which resulted in a -6 goal difference and shipping 8 goals in their three matches. The Americans managed to score early and often both in the World Cup and in the recent friendlies. That habit will be useful against a team like Haiti who struggles to come back from falling behind or with keeping leads for that matter. A USA win should be in the cards for this one and if an early goal comes there may very well be more to follow.

nigeria.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes rejects second contract offer
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected the club’s second offer to extend his contract, leaving negotiations over the Portugal midfielder’s future unresolved. BBC Sport reports that Fernandes is out of contract at the end of the season, although United can extend his deal by 12 months, until 2028. The club wants to agree a new contract before using that option. If no agreement is reached, United are expected to trigger the extension before January 1. Without it, Fernandes would be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs from that date, with six months remaining on his deal. It is unclear when Fernandes rejected the offer. A resolution does not appear imminent amid the upheaval at Old Trafford: Michael Carrick was sacked on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to take over as head coach. United will hope Pochettino’s arrival can persuade Fernandes to stay. The midfielder came close to joining Pochettino’s Tottenham in 2019, before moving from Sporting to United six months later. He has scored six goals in 13 appearances for United this season. BBC chief football news reporter Simon Stone says Fernandes wants to compete for the biggest prizes and will want to see what impact Pochettino has at United. The club, meanwhile, must weigh the cost and length of a new deal against Fernandes’ recent drop in form after an outstanding previous season, when he broke the Premier League assists record and won major player-of-the-year awards. Fernandes is 32, and a new contract could commit United to a substantial outlay over several years. Both sides may therefore have reasons to take their time, despite the club’s wish to keep its captain. nigeria.title: Meet the US family with five generations born on the same date
nigeria.description: An American family has entered the Guinness World Records after five consecutive generations were born on the same date, September 14, in a remarkable family coincidence spanning more than a century. The Bell and Harlow family secured the record for the most generations born on the same day after the arrival of baby Arthur Bell on September 14, 2025. Arthur’s birth extended a family tradition that began with his great-great-grandfather, Wilber Harlow, who was born on September 14, 1907. The other family members who share the birthday are Wilber’s daughter, Addie Harlow, born on September 14, 1949; his grandson, Donald Harlow, born on September 14, 1972; and his great-granddaughter, Emma Bell, born on September 14, 1997. Emma is Arthur’s mother, while Donald is his grandfather. According to Guinness World Records, the family surpassed the previous record of four generations born on the same date, which had been jointly held by seven families. The family said they had been aware of the unusual coincidence when four generations shared the September 14 birthday but delayed applying for official recognition because they hoped another child would continue the tradition. Their wish came true when Emma’s second child, Arthur, arrived on the expected date, extending the record to five generations. Speaking about the achievement, Emma said the family had always known they could hold the record but wanted to wait until they had a fifth generation. “We kind of always knew that we held a record with four generations, we just never applied because we had that ambition to have the fifth on 14 September,” she said. “And then it worked out!” She added that the family was delighted to become the sole record holders rather than share the title with other families. Arthur’s grandfather, Donald, also expressed his excitement, saying: “God works in beautiful ways.” The family’s birthday tradition began in 1907 when Wilber Harlow was born. He later worked as a postmaster and owned the Harlow General Store in Brooks, Iowa. On September 14, 1949, Wilber and his wife welcomed their daughter, Addie, on his birthday, beginning the remarkable sequence. Addie later worked as a secretary for the Chief of Police in La Vista, Nebraska, for more than 20 years. Her son, Donald, continued the coincidence when he was born on the same date in 1972. Donald subsequently welcomed Emma, who also arrived on September 14, 1997. Emma and her husband, Wyatt, said they became particularly excited when they realised their second child’s expected arrival date was September 14. nigeria.title: U-23 AFCONQ: Nigeria suffer 2-0 defeat to DR Congo in first leg
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations suffered a setback on Friday after the Olympic Eagles lost 2-0 to DR Congo in the first leg of their second-round qualifying tie. The Nigerian side, led by Ikorodu City head coach Bright Osehai Ozebagbe and former Nigeria U-20 assistant coach Deniran Ortega, struggled to convert their early opportunities as the hosts secured a comfortable advantage ahead of the return fixture. The coaching duo took charge in the absence of Super Eagles manager Eric Chelle, who was occupied with Nigeria’s senior national team preparations for their crucial Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. Nigeria started brightly and nearly took the lead in the fourth minute when Victor Samuel’s effort missed the target. The midfielder had another opportunity five minutes later after finding himself one-on-one with the DR Congo goalkeeper but failed to convert. The missed chances proved costly as DR Congo took the lead in the 20th minute in controversial circumstances. Nigeria goalkeeper Samuel James appeared to have been fouled by a Congolese player while attempting to collect an aerial ball during the build-up to the opening goal. However, the referee allowed the goal to stand. The Olympic Eagles suffered another setback in the 30th minute when Brighton youngster Zadok Yohanna was forced off with an injury. DR Congo doubled their advantage five minutes before the break through Felozefe Mabete, who produced an impressive free-kick to put the hosts firmly in control. Despite their attempts to find a way back into the contest after the restart, Nigeria could not break down the Congolese defence, with the hosts protecting their two-goal advantage until the final whistle. The result leaves the Olympic Eagles with a difficult task in the second leg, as they must overturn the deficit to keep their qualification hopes alive. Nigeria will host DR Congo in the return fixture at the Remo Stars Stadium on Tuesday, where they will seek to secure an aggregate victory and advance to the final qualifying round. The Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations also serves as the qualification pathway for the men’s football tournament at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. nigeria.title: Boko Haram: Zulum announces ₦50k for each soldier deployed to Borno communities
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities of Maiwa and Koshebe villages. Our Correspondent report that Koshebe in November 28, 2020 came under massacre when some armed Boko Haram militants launched a devastating attack on peasant and laborer rice farmers working in the fields (near Zabarmari and Maiduguri), where over 100 farm laborers—many of whom traveled from Sokoto State in northwest Nigeria for seasonal harvest work—were rounded up, tied, and their throats slit. Likewise, in November, 2023, suspected Boko Haram insurgents again targeted rice farmers harvesting crops in the Karkut and Koshebe general areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 farmers and leaving others missing. But Zulum assured that he will provide the needed support to strengthen security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, ensure safe travel, and revive trade in communities recovering from years of insurgency. The Governor gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. The highway links communities along the corridor to markets and facilitates the movement of agricultural produce, essential commodities and other goods. Zulum said improving security along the route would help residents travel safely, trade and rebuild their livelihoods. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe villages, the governor pledged “to provide operational logistics and sustain welfare support. He announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities”. Governor Zulum’s administration has consistently supported military operations with logistics and welfare assistance as part of efforts to improve security and help displaced residents return to their communities. The Governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. nigeria.title: Conversion to university: We are waiting for release of government gazette – Abdul, YABATECH Rector
nigeria.description: By Adesina Wahab The conversion of Yaba College of Technology, YABATECH, to the Federal University of Technology and Vocational Studies is being delayed because the Federal Government is yet to release the official gazette that would convey that, the Rector, Dr Ibraheem Abdul, has disclosed. He stated this on Friday while answering questions on the sideline of the press briefing to herald the 38th convocation ceremonies of the College. “We are pretty much on course to becoming a University. The bill has been passed by the National Assembly and it has been signed into law by President Bola Tinubu. At our end, we are adequately prepared. What remains now is for the official gazette to be released by the Federal Government. When that is done, the institutional evaluation will be conducted by the Federal Ministry of Education and then the National Universities Commission, NUC, would come and accredit our courses. “Indeed, this historic conversion reflects the growing recognition by the President and the larger society of the importance of technology-driven and Vocational education in addressing Nigeria’s human-capital and industrial development needs,” he said. As part of the convocation ceremonies, Dr Abdul said the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, the Minister of Finance, Mr Taiwo Oyedele and Mrs Itunu Omotayo would be conferred Fellowship of the College. Also, Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Hamzat, will deliver the convocation lecture titled ” From silos to synergy: Reimagining Nigeria’s tertiary education system for national transformation”. The event will be chaired by the Minister of State for Education, Prof.Suwaiba Ahmad. Giving a breakdown of the number of graduating students, the Rector said a total of 10,886 would be involved. Out of the figure, 361 are graduating with distinction, 3,160 earned upper credit pass, 5,696 are graduating with lower credit pass and 1,669 have pass grade. Abdul added that the College has continued to promote entrepreneurship as an essential component of its education philosophy and that the citing of the Folawiyo Entrepreneurship Centre in the College was a testament to that . nigeria.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in alleged $4.5bn fraud trial
nigeria.description: An Ikeja Special Offences Court on Friday admitted a certified copy of a Supreme Court judgment linking former CBN Governor, Godwin Emefiele, to forfeited properties. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. The Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo (SAN), had tendered the document through EFCC investigator, Mr Alvan Gurumnaan. However, Emefiele’s lead counsel, Mr Ojo Olalekan (SAN), opposed its admissibility, arguing that only four justices signed the judgment. He maintained that Supreme Court decisions were ordinarily delivered by panels of five or seven justices. Ojo also argued that the judgment arose from non-conviction forfeiture proceedings and was irrelevant to the prosecution’s case. Counsel to Omoile, Mr Adeyinka Kotoye (SAN), aligned himself with the objections and urged the court to reject the document. Kotoye argued that admitting the judgment could undermine the principle of estoppel and the defendants’ presumption of innocence. He also questioned the prosecution’s decision to introduce the document after proceedings had begun. Responding, Oyedepo argued that the document was a duly certified Supreme Court decision admissible under Sections 102 and 104 of the Evidence Act. Following the ruling, Gurumnaan faced cross-examination by Emefiele’s counsel over his role in the investigation. The witness said he personally obtained statements, analysed bank statements and coordinated other members of the investigation team. He confirmed interviewing Zenith Bank Managing Director, Dr Ebenezer Onyeagwu, but could not immediately recall whether a statement was obtained. Gurumnaan said the investigation involved hundreds of interviews with CBN officials, commercial bank employees and personnel of other government agencies. nigeria.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
nigeria.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. The matter also attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), which arraigned her over alleged offences connected to the fundraising campaign. She pleaded not guilty to the charges. Vanguard News The post Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The incumbent member representing Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency of Zamfara State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) court-ordered fresh primary election with 26,646 votes. Jaji defeated two other aspirants in the rerun conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, to reclaim the party’s ticket after his earlier nomination was nullified by the Federal High Court in Abuja. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the exercise, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the Kaura Namoda Collation Centre after the conclusion of voting and collation across the two local government areas. According to the committee, the constituency had 42,266 registered APC members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited, while 27,359 votes were recorded as total votes cast. Jaji’s closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, polled 713 votes, while the third contestant, Musa Zubairu, failed to secure any vote. A breakdown of the results showed that Jaji won in both local government areas, polling 14,264 votes in Kaura Namoda against Dangaladima’s 465, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji, Jaji secured 12,382 votes, compared with Dangaladima’s 248 votes, while Zubairu again failed to record any vote. Declaring the results, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and the party’s guidelines governing primary elections. “Having satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and guidelines, I hereby declare Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji the winner of the fresh primary election,” he announced. The rerun followed a legal challenge instituted by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court in Abuja against Jaji’s earlier emergence as the party’s candidate for the constituency. The court nullified the earlier nomination and directed the APC to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The party’s national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the exercise in compliance with the court’s directive. Jaji, who is associated with the political camp of the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has now secured the party’s ticket through the court-ordered process. The outcome settles the party’s immediate nomination contest in the constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the legal dispute over its earlier primary election. nigeria.title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Report No fewer than 53 Nigerians were among 112 undocumented African nationals arrested by Malaysian immigration authorities between January and October 31 over various immigration offences, Malaysian newspaper, Utusan Malaysia, has reported. The Nigerians recorded the highest number of arrests among the African nationals, followed by Uganda with 13, Kenya with 10 and Ghana with eight. The Director-General of Malaysia’s Immigration Department, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, disclosed the figures in an interview with Utusan Malaysia, published on Friday. According to the report, other nationals arrested included Somalia (6), Tanzania (6), Senegal (4), Algeria (3), Burkina Faso (2), Togo (2) and The Gambia (2). One national each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also arrested. Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, contrary to Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. He said 85 people were arrested for the offence, including 47 Nigerians. “The primary offence recorded is entering and remaining in the country without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63; this resulted in 85 arrests, 47 of which involved Nigerian nationals,” he said. The immigration chief said 23 others were arrested for overstaying their permitted period under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act. He added that three people were detained for violating the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested for allegedly possessing forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act. The authorities also arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid immigration passes. Shaaban said the enforcement operations were part of efforts to curb undocumented migration and prosecute employers who engage or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. “These ongoing enforcement operations reflect the authorities’ steadfast commitment to curbing the presence of undocumented migrants and taking firm action against any employers who harbor or employ them,” he said. However, the report did not disclose the identities of the Nigerians arrested or the specific locations where the arrests were made. nigeria.title: 2027: Wike Criticises Obi Over National Anthem Snub At NDC Lagos Town Hall Meeting

Wike made these remarks on Friday, during a stakeholders’ town hall meeting in Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State, organised under the banner of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates. ﻿ Addressing traditional rulers, community leaders, youths, and party faithful, the FCT minister argued that a leader who disregards national symbols cannot be trusted with the presidency. “A whole national anthem of a country is being sung. A man who wants to be President of Nigeria would disobey and sit down. And then not only that, when a different national anthem that is not being used for Nigeria [was sung], he stood up. “In a way, he does not belong to this country. In a way, he has said he does not belong to this country; that if you give him the president, he would do a different thing that will divide Nigeria. “A man who does not believe in Nigeria, someone who derives joy in ridiculing the country by disrespecting its symbolic National Anthem must not be allowed to come near the presidency of our country,” the minister said. Wike further criticised Obi’s political trajectory and past governance record, alleging that the former Anambra State governor frequently abandons political parties whenever internal crises arise, rather than staying to resolve them. He also faulted Obi for not conducting local government elections during his eight-year tenure as governor, describing it as a contradiction to his professed belief in the rule of law. Tackles Atiku, Amaechi In addition to targeting Obi, the FCT Minister took aim at the opposition coalition involving former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi. Wike questioned their track records in public office, specifically citing the state of seaports during Amaechi’s tenure as Minister of Transportation and alleging that the administration demolished Government Secondary School, Ogu, without rebuilding it, alongside unfulfilled promises regarding a 1,000-bed specialist hospital. Urging the people of Ogu-Bolo to disregard what he termed “big grammar” from opposition politicians on television, Wike maintained that President Bola Tinubu’s administration had delivered tangible dividends of democracy to the area. He pointed to the construction of the Ogu-Bolo Civic Centre—facilitated through the federal appointment of an indigene, Boma Iyaye—as well as the conduct of local government elections. nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Footballers are often praised for keeping their cool when the stakes are high, but some of the game’s most recognisable names have become known for receiving repeated red cards. From tough-tackling defenders to forceful midfielders, their careers have combined success on the pitch with frequent disciplinary woes. Gerardo Bedoya stands clear at the top of the ranking, with 46 red cards during his playing career and recognised by the Guinness World Records. The former Colombia international’s fiery reputation followed him into coaching: in 2016, he was sent off just 21 minutes into his first match as an assistant coach at Santa Fe. Red-card totals can differ between databases because no single global record tracks every player’s dismissals across all competitions. Alexis Ruano Delgado — 22 red cards The Spanish centre-back played for Málaga, Getafe, Valencia and Sevilla, among other clubs. He won the Copa del Rey with Valencia in 2008. Six of his red cards came during his time at Barcelona. Cyril Rool — 22 red cards The French midfielder played in Ligue 1 for clubs including Lens, Bordeaux and Nice. His career, which ran from 1993 to 2010, also included more than 150 yellow cards. Gerardo Torrado — 22 red cards Mexico’s former defensive midfielder earned 144 international caps and played at three World Cups. He spent 11 years at Cruz Azul, where he was sent off 14 times. nigeria.title: NIS moves to prevent foreign interference in 2027 elections
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) and other stakeholders have convened to strategise measures to prevent interference by foreign elements in the upcoming 2027 general elections. The NIS, the Department of State Services (DSS), the Border Communities Development Agency (BCDA) and other stakeholders convened at a sensitisation workshop at the NIS headquarters on Friday in Abuja. The workshop is themed: “The Role of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Election Monitoring and Management.” Speaking at the workshop, the NIS Comptroller-General, Mrs Kemi Nandap, said that the successful conduct of the upcoming elections required institutional cooperation from all security stakeholders. Nandap, represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Mrs Franca Nwanneka, said that the deliberation was important as the general election is fast approaching. “Beyond the responsibility of conducting credible elections, there is the equally important task of providing a peaceful and secure environment in which the democratic process can thrive. “Achieving this requires collective vigilance, effective coordination and the commitment of all institutions entrusted with safeguarding our nation,” she said. According to her, the NIS occupied a strategic position in the nation’s security architecture as the agency saddled with the responsibility and mandate of border security and migration management. “We must therefore remain alert to the influx of foreigners, emerging threats, particularly irregular migration and smuggling of migrants. “We must also be on high alert to trafficking in persons and other transnational criminal activities capable of undermining national security,” she said. Nandap also reaffirmed the NIS’ stance as a non-partisan service loyal to the Constitution and the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and warned officers against using official capabilities to participate in politics. She charged officers to demonstrate the highest standards of political neutrality, discipline and respect for the rule of law. The CG charged senior officers, zonal coordinators, comptrollers, and heads of formations to ensure that every command is adequately prepared before, during and after the elections. She emphasised strengthened surveillance, intelligence gathering, effective deployment and close coordination with relevant security agencies as key areas that could facilitate credible elections. “No single agency can address the complex security challenges confronting our nation in isolation. Our collective strength lies in our ability to work together, share timely information and respond decisively to emerging threats. “I look forward to even stronger collaboration as we approach the elections because the task of securing our nation and sustaining public confidence in our institutions is a collective responsibility,” she added. nigeria.title: 2027: Adebutu hails court ruling, says justice has prevailed
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has hailed the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, directing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to restore his name to the list of candidates for the forthcoming governorship election within 24 hours. Adebutu described the judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu on Friday, as a victory for justice, the rule of law and democratic principles. Relief is here!” He described the judgment as a significant development in the legal battle over his exclusion from INEC’s published list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun State governorship election. Adebutu said he had consistently maintained that his PDP membership, registration and emergence as the party’s governorship candidate were legitimate and in accordance with due process. “From the moment my name was omitted from INEC’s published list, I maintained that the facts surrounding my PDP membership, registration and the process that produced me as the party’s governorship candidate were clear,” he said. According to him, the party remained confident in the strength of its position and resolved to pursue the matter through the appropriate legal channels. He noted that the judgment had reaffirmed the importance of due process, stressing that political and electoral disputes should be determined on their merits rather than on speculation or premature conclusions. Adebutu expressed appreciation to the national leadership of the PDP, particularly Chief Nyesom Wike, whom he described as the party’s national leader, and its National Chairman, Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed, for their support and confidence throughout the legal proceedings. nigeria.title: Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking
nigeria.description: Michael Carrick wished Manchester United “nothing but success” 24 hours after he was sacked, reaffirming his enduring love for the club, who have already appointed Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal, but results have nose-dived in this campaign. The Red Devils are in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far. The Old Trafford club named former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino, currently USA head coach, as their new manager on Friday. Despite the downturn this season, Carrick remained popular with supporters in part for his role as a player in multiple triumphs under Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013. The 45-year-old said his affection remained rock-solid. “I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change,” Carrick wrote in an Instagram post. “I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. “I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.” The former England midfielder paid tribute to the fans, his coaching staff and United’s players. “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love,” he wrote. “There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. “It’s different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time. “It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.” Carrick described United’s fans as a “special, rare breed”. “We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember,” he said. “The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time. “I just wanted to give you something back. nigeria.title: FG Signs Port Harcourt Airport Concession Agreement, Assures Workers’ Protection
nigeria.description: The Federal Government has signed a concession agreement for the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt, with PH Airport Limited, following assurances from the concessionaire that the arrangement would not lead to job losses. The agreement was signed at the office of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, in Abuja, on Thursday. The Federal Government delegation was led by Keyamo, while PH Airport Limited was represented by its Group Managing Director, Eyo Asuquo. The signing followed a meeting between the minister and aviation union leaders to discuss the implications of the concession for airport workers. Speaking on behalf of the unions, Comrade Ben Nnabue said organised labour had approved the agreement after receiving assurances that no aviation worker would lose their job as a result of the arrangement. He said job security remained a major concern for the unions and that they were satisfied with the commitments made before endorsing the agreement. Photo of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and the federal government delegation in Abuja, on Thursday. Also speaking, Asuquo highlighted Port Harcourt’s strategic importance in the Gulf of Guinea, describing the airport as a potential gateway for regional commerce, investment and connectivity. He said PH Airport Limited intended to improve the airport’s infrastructure and operational standards, adding that the concession would create more employment opportunities rather than result in job losses. According to him, the company’s vision extends beyond managing the facility to expanding airport-related activities, attracting investment and unlocking its economic potential. The Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, Chris Najomo; Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; ministry directors and aviation union leaders attended the event. The concession agreement was subsequently signed by the concessionaire and relevant ministry officials, with Keyamo presiding over the ceremony. The Federal Government said the agreement was part of its broader efforts to attract private-sector investment and expertise into the development and management of Nigeria’s airport infrastructure. Under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development has pursued reforms aimed at modernising airports, improving operational efficiency and strengthening the aviation sector’s contribution to economic growth. The Port Harcourt airport concession is expected to improve the passenger experience, strengthen airport services, and attract investment to the facility. nigeria.title: Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the attack on the party’s supporters at a town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday, urging them to remain peaceful while defending their democratic rights. Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Friday, a day after suspected thugs disrupted the party’s gathering in Oregun, Lagos. He said he had been informed that a group of thugs mobilised to attack participants who arrived early for the meeting, noting that he had travelled to Lagos from Abuja to attend a commendation service for Chief Sir Okey Ezibe before proceeding to join supporters at the town hall meeting. “The political violence being enabled by certain political actors against our supporters is an ill wind that blows no one any good. Anarchy consumes everyone,” he said. “We will remain law-abiding, even in the face of extreme provocation.” Obi said the town hall meeting went ahead despite the disruption and participants raised concerns about reviving the economy, the high cost of living, corruption, insecurity, support for vulnerable citizens and the integrity of elections. He said the first responsibility of any government was to secure the country and unite its people around a shared purpose. He also pledged that his administration would pursue policies to reduce living costs, improve welfare and invest in healthcare and education. On the forthcoming elections, the former Anambra governor said protecting the integrity of the process was a shared responsibility, saying the NDC would deploy agents to polling units to observe and document voting, ward collation and the final declaration of results. “I encouraged our people to eschew violence while remaining peaceful, vigilant, and resolute in defending their democratic rights,” he said. Vanguard reported that suspected political thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones invaded the Oregun rally on Thursday, attacking supporters and injuring some participants, although Obi was not at the rally when the incident occurred. nigeria.title: Is Galadima the Round Peg in the Round Hole for Adamawa?
nigeria.description: In Nigerian politics, the phrase “a round peg in a round hole” is often used to suggest that a candidate’s temperament, experience and timing align perfectly with the demands of the moment. In Adamawa State, that description is increasingly being attached to Ahmed Tijjani Galadima, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for 2027. But is he truly the right fit for Adamawa’s complex political and developmental realities, or simply the beneficiary of strategic party consensus? Adamawa is no ordinary political battleground. Situated in Nigeria’s North-East, the state has long balanced agricultural potential with security challenges, urban expansion with rural neglect, and a politically vibrant electorate with shifting party loyalties. Governorship contests here are rarely predictable. Personal networks, regional considerations, grassroots mobilisation and elite consensus all play decisive roles—and often collide. Galadima’s emergence as the APC’s standard-bearer was no accident. A seasoned technocrat, he previously served as Executive Secretary of the Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a position that placed him at the intersection of public administration, human capital development and federal policymaking. Within policy circles, that experience is often cited as evidence of administrative competence—a quality many voters say has become increasingly important after years of governance characterised more by political brinkmanship than institutional reform. Within the APC, his candidacy also represents consolidation. Several key aspirants stepped aside before and during the primary process, sparing the party the bruising internal contest that has weakened it in previous election cycles. For a party seeking to reclaim power in Adamawa from the administration of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, unity is more than desirable; it is essential. Galadima’s ability to attract support across competing blocs suggests he enjoys both political goodwill and strategic alliances. Yet politics in Adamawa extends beyond party arithmetic. The electorate remains deeply concerned about security, particularly in communities affected by the spillover of insurgency in the North-East. Farmers want safer farmlands, traders need secure transport corridors, and young people seek economic opportunities that do not require leaving the state. Any candidate seeking to be regarded as the “right fit” must present credible solutions to these interconnected challenges. Supporters argue that Galadima’s administrative experience positions him to drive economic renewal. Adamawa’s economy remains largely agrarian, with significant untapped potential in agro-processing, livestock production and cross-border trade with neighbouring Cameroon. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners. The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas. Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them. Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day. “When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.” A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node. The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says. The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double Crypto trading on Robinhood fell by almost half from a year ago in October, the company said Thursday , as customers traded $17 billion of digital assets while their bets on event contracts more than doubled. The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025. Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year. Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025. Event contracts take off as crypto cools The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts. Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier. Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. business.title: President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them. Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported. Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber. Who the nominees are Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules. Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance. Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High Bitcoin price traded near $69,800 on Friday morning after briefly crashing to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern, its lowest level since mid-August, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The rebound held after October producer prices rose less than economists had expected, though the U.S. dollar remained near a 19-month high and traders still fully priced a December Federal Reserve rate hike. Bitcoin price was trading near $72,800 at this time Thursday. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then gave way late at night, breaking below $70,000 and sliding to that midnight low. The move also pushed the bitcoin price below its 200-week moving average , a long-term trend line near $68,000. Buyers lifted it back above $69,000 before sunrise, and the rebound extended toward $69,800 after the producer-price report. A stronger dollar and higher yields weigh on the bitcoin price The U.S. Dollar Index held above 103 Friday after a three-day rally took it to its highest level since April 2025. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.15% ahead of the data, and two-year yields, which track Fed expectations most closely, were on pace for their worst week since 2024, Bloomberg reported. Traders still see an 88% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting and a 12% chance of a half-point move, CME FedWatch data show . Fed Governor Christopher Waller has added a 50-basis-point increase to the discussion, and New York Fed President John Williams said Thursday that inflation remains high and policymakers need to take further action. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar tends to drain demand for risk assets. Both have pressured the bitcoin price since this week’s hotter-than-expected consumer price index. Bitcoin has also broken from tech stocks. It fell 5.9% between Nov. 5 and Nov. 12 while the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.4%, a sign it is trading more on yields and the dollar than on the AI trade. Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.6% Friday after the producer-price report, as investors also weighed Nvidia’s announcement that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Digital Credit: Comparing The Six Bitcoin Preferred Stocks Digital credit is an emerging asset class that transforms corporate Bitcoin balance sheets into income producing securities. Strategy pioneered the market with five perpetual preferred equity instruments: STRK, STRF, STRD, STRC, and STRE (the first four are listed in the U.S.). Strive subsequently introduced SATA and SATS, bringing the category to six U.S. instruments across two issuers. These securities offer investors preferred equity (read: credit-like) exposure to companies whose balance sheets are dominated by Bitcoin. Their perpetual structure means investors principally rely on recurring dividends and the continued financial strength of the issuer. Unlike term debt, there is no maturation date at which the full principal is ever paid back. Evaluating digital credit requires examining four characteristics: creditworthiness, investor protections, liquidity, and dividend profile. This article explains all four dimensions and then offers a ranking for the six digital credit instruments along these lines. None of this should be taken as investment advice—it is only a systematic framework for analyzing digital credit. 1. Creditworthiness Creditworthiness measures an issuer’s ability to support its financial obligations. Traditional credit analysis focuses on earnings, free cash flow, and refinancing capacity. Companies with strong cash generation can service interest and repay maturing debt. Digital credit issuers today derive financial strength primarily from their Bitcoin reserves, placing greater emphasis on net asset coverage. In the future we could certainly see digital credit issuers that also have significant cash flows on top of Bitcoin holdings, which would add to creditworthiness. The central question is how much Bitcoin supports each dollar of credit obligations. One useful measure is the BTC Rating , which compares the dollar value of Bitcoin reserves with the outstanding credit, accounting for the seniority of each credit instrument. Cash reserves can further strengthen creditworthiness by reducing net obligations. For example, a 5x BTC Rating indicates five dollars of Bitcoin supporting every dollar of notional credit claims. Higher ratings provide greater protection against Bitcoin price declines. Seniority matters because instruments from the same issuer can have different claims on the same asset base. A senior preferred instrument benefits from greater coverage than a junior preferred instrument: all senior claims are included in the BTC Rating calculation of a junior instrument. Creditworthiness also depends on corporate governance and capital allocation. Management must preserve sufficient Bitcoin coverage while funding recurring dividends. entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed.
